chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said:
Betake to noble character (makarim al-akhlaq), for God Mighty and Majestic loves it. And beware of blameworthy actions, for God Mighty and Majestic hates them.

Betake to reciting the Quran, for the degrees of Paradise are proportionate to the verses of the Quran; on the Day of Resurrection the reciter of the Quran will be told: 'Recite and ascend,' and each time he recites a verse, he ascends a degree.
Betake to beautiful character, for it brings its possessor to the rank of one who fasts and stands (in night prayer). And betake to good neighbourliness, for God has commanded it.
Betake to the tooth stick (siwak), for it is a purifier and a beautiful tradition. Betake to God's obligations and fulfill them. And beware of God's prohibitions and abstain from them.

key_terms.السواك: The tooth stick (siwak/miswak) — a branch or twig used to clean the teeth, considered both a purifier and a prophetic sunnah.
key_terms.حسن الخلق: Beautiful/good character (husn al-khuluq) — inner moral excellence, said to raise one to the rank of those who fast and perform night prayers.
key_terms.فرائض الله: God's obligations — the mandatory religious duties that must be performed.
key_terms.محارم الله: God's prohibitions — the forbidden things that must be avoided.
key_terms.مذام الأفعال: Blameworthy/vile actions — actions despised by God, the moral opposites of makarim al-akhlaq.
key_terms.مكارم الأخلاق: Noble character traits — the highest moral virtues, contrasted with mādhamm al-af'āl (blameworthy actions). A foundational concept in Shia ethical literature.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about noble character, Quran recitation, and good neighbourliness?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a comprehensive ethical exhortation through a chain ending at al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, his trusted companion. The hadith presents eight imperatives covering both virtues to embrace — noble character, Quran recitation, good character, neighbourliness, and the siwak — and obligations to fulfill and prohibitions to avoid. The teaching reflects al-Sadiq's characteristic style of comprehensive moral instruction that integrates individual spiritual practice with social ethics, delivered to an audience familiar with the Imam's method of pairing divine love and hatred as motivators for moral conduct.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi from his father Muhammad b. Khalid from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
Betake to noble character (makarim al-akhlaq), for Allah loves it. Beware of evil actions, for Allah hates them.

Betake to reciting the Quran, for the degrees of Paradise are proportionate to the verses of the Quran. On the Day of Resurrection, a reciter will be told: “Recite and climb”, and when he recites a verse, he will climb a degree.
Betake to beautiful character, because that will take one to the rank of one who is fasting and standing [in prayer]. Betake to beautiful neighbourliness, for surely, Allah ordered that.
Betake to the tooth stick, for it is a purifier and a beautiful tradition. Betake to what Allah has obligated and fulfill them. Beware of what Allah has prohibited and abstain from them.
